title: Net Displacement as Accumulated Area
caption_md: Here $v(t)=2\sin(t)$ is a velocity function. Drag the right endpoint $x$ to sweep across the interval and watch the shaded area grow — that shaded region equals the net displacement $\int_0^x v(t)\,dt$. Notice how the accumulated value **increases** when $v(t)>0$ (moving forward) and **decreases** when $v(t)<0$ (moving backward). At $x=\pi$ you have maximum displacement; by $x=2\pi$ the positive and negative areas cancel and net displacement returns to 0.
